Category C+E training

Trailer training for drivers who already hold Category C and need the articulated or drawbar entitlement.

In plain English

Category C+E adds a trailer to the rigid entitlement. It is the licence used for articulated lorries and for drawbar combinations. It is not the first step up from a car licence.

Who it is for

Drivers who already hold Category C and need to add the trailer entitlement.

What it covers

  • Articulated goods vehicles
  • Rigid lorries towing a drawbar trailer

The unit and the trailer are not named on this demonstration.

Eligibility and prerequisites

General guidance, not a check of your licence.

  • Category C is the usual entitlement held before C+E training
  • The licence you hold is checked before training is arranged
  • Any medical or theory steps that still apply are explained at that point
  • This page is general guidance. It does not confirm eligibility for an individual

What the training includes

  • Coupling and uncoupling
  • Reversing and manoeuvres with a trailer
  • On-road driving with the combination
  • Guidance on what the practical test involves

How the course works

  1. Enquire about Category C+E

    Say which course you want, which base you prefer, and how you would like to be contacted.

  2. Check the licence you hold

    The current entitlement is checked before training is arranged. This page does not confirm eligibility.

  3. Train in the vehicle

    Practical time covers the vehicle, the manoeuvres and the road driving.

  4. Prepare for the practical test

    How the test is booked is explained when you enquire. This site does not claim a result.

Training format

Yard work for coupling, uncoupling and reversing, then on-road driving. Offered at the example bases that list Category C+E.

Duration and cost

How long the training takes is confirmed when you enquire.

Ask for a quote. No fee is listed on this page. Medicals, theory tests and the practical test are separate costs.

Questions about this course

Do I need Category C before C+E?

Category C is the usual entitlement held before trailer training. If you do not hold it yet, start with Category C.

Where is Category C+E listed?

At the Bristol and Exeter example bases. It is not listed at Taunton.

Guides

  • Category C vs Category C+ECategory C and Category C+E are both goods-vehicle entitlements. One is the rigid lorry. The other adds a trailer. They are trained and tested separately.
  • What happens on an HGV driving test?The practical test checks that you can control the vehicle and drive it on the road. The detail is set by DVSA and can be updated, so treat this as an outline and check the official description before test day.
  • Which HGV licence do I need?The licence depends on the vehicle you want to drive, and on what you already hold. This guide separates the main goods-vehicle entitlements from Driver CPC. It does not confirm that you qualify.
